notes: Dev-split TBox expansion paired with physics-replace-d005 ("Every Type II supernova is the explosion of a brown dwarf."): the revised rule's new conclusion (has_progenitor, a brown dwarf) given to a made-up class under a real one (fictional: subject): the Velkarin supernova, a new class of supernova. It cannot sit under Type II itself, since every real Type II supernova comes from a massive star and the insert would then contradict a stored rule (a replace, not an insert). PHYSICALLY IMPOSSIBLE CONCLUSION, recorded here (the schema has no flag; report results on this record apart): the paired conclusion is physically impossible (a brown dwarf never ignites hydrogen, so nothing known makes it explode); the insert contradicts no recorded fact about a named thing, but it does go against general stellar physics, as the revision does. Changed in review: the prompts ask "what kind of object" rather than "what kind of star", because a brown dwarf is a substellar object (Wikipedia) and "star" implies hydrogen fusion, which set the prompt's own word against the bridge of the first derived question; the paired revision (d005, final) keeps "star", so the direct and paraphrase wording differ from it on purpose. The pair is not changed to another revision because the pairing is fixed by the README (d002 with d005). A made-up class has no members a model knows, so the README's "applies it to a member the model already knows" cannot hold here: two derived questions instead follow the rule to the new conclusion and look up a stored fact about brown dwarfs (composition, 2 hops: no hydrogen fusion in the core; less massive than the Sun), and the third names an unnamed member in the prompt and asks what to look for in archival images (inheritance, application), mirroring the revision's third question. The mass question separates the edit from a default: a model that ignores the insert and assumes a usual core-collapse progenitor answers "more massive". Near unrelated: the progenitor of a Type II supernova (a massive star), which differs from the new answer and catches an insert that spreads to supernovae in general. The Crab Nebula side facts, checks and evidence are the revision's. The new object is fixed by the paired revision (d005, final), so the insert cannot be made more plausible by changing it; a possible but wrong object (a white dwarf, a Wolf-Rayet star) in both records would remove the problem.
